name: Micro Shift
description: A copy a few cents sharp on the left and a few cents flat on the right, each a few milliseconds late: makes one source wide and thick with no chorus sweep.

params.name: Detune
params.description: How far the two copies are tuned away from the dry sound: the left one sharp, the right one flat. A few cents is a soft widening; higher settings beat against the dry sound and turn sour.

params.name: Delay
params.description: How far behind the dry sound the copies sit, the right one a little later than the left. Short settings fuse with the source; long ones are heard as a doubled take.

params.name: Drift
params.description: Lets the tuning and timing of each copy wander slowly and at random. At zero the copies hold perfectly still; higher settings sway like a worn tape.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Feeds each copy back into itself, so it is detuned again on every pass: the left side climbs and the right side sinks as the repeats fade.

params.name: Focus
params.description: Everything below this stays dry and in the centre, so the bass keeps its weight. Raise it to widen only the upper part of the sound.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Rolls the treble off the two copies. Lower settings tuck them behind the dry sound as a soft halo; with Feedback up, each repeat gets darker.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far apart the two copies sit. At full they are hard left and right; at zero both are in the centre and the effect thickens without widening.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry sound and the two copies. The sound below Focus stays at full level wherever this is set.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Models the micro pitch shift treatment of studio harmonizers in outline (a slightly sharp copy on one side, a slightly flat copy on the other, each a few milliseconds late), not any unit. Each copy is a delay-line pitch shifter with a single read head, spliced by normalised cross-correlation as in the autocorrelation splice of US patent 4,464,784 (expired) and in Verhelst and Roelands, 'An overlap-add technique based on waveform similarity (WSOLA) for high quality time-scale modification of speech' (ICASSP 1993); splices also wait for a stretch of the line with no attack in it. Reads use a 16-tap Kaiser-windowed sinc.
